PagerBot: ALERT: slo_burnrate_high | route=/embed | windows=[30s:0.18, 5m:0.08, 1h:0.02] | burn_budget=0.05
Nina (on-call): saw that. 30s spike is pretty sharp in eu-central-1, p95 latency up and some 504s showing in the logs.
DeployBot: DEPLOY: priya/adaptive-batching -> canary(20%) @ 2026-03-15T09:15:00Z tag=adaptive-batching-2026-03-15
Priya (ENG-PLATFORM): confirming canary started at 09:15 UTC, targeting eu-central-1. We pushed an adaptive batching change to try and reduce tail latency.
Raj (SRE): can we correlate the spike with batch size changes? adaptive batching might increase instantaneous load to redis queue workers.
Tom (Support): I have three tickets opened reporting timeouts for embedding jobs since ~09:18 UTC, all eu-central-1 customers. Low impact but visible.
Nina (on-call): quick check of infra: redis connection pool exhaustion traces on embed-queue-host-12. connection_retries and backpressure observed.
Priya (ENG-PLATFORM): that host is in the canary shard set for the rollout. we only rolled 20% but that includes a hot host. rolling back to 0% now.
Raj (SRE): suggestion: make 30s window metric non-pager (ticket only) so ops aren't paged for extremely short-lived spikes, keep 5m/1h as paging windows. We still want visibility but avoid waking people for transient deploy tremors.
Nina (on-call): agree. also add a short-term suppression for redis-specific transient errors so they don't trigger paging while we triage. we'll still log and ticket.
Priya (ENG-PLATFORM): rollback in progress -> canary -> 0% at 09:22 UTC. should start rebalancing traffic in ~20s.
Raj (SRE): patch draft for alert mapping below — applying to staging first:

```
# slo_burnrate_high patch v1
route: /embed
windows: [30s, 5m, 1h]
thresholds:
  30s: 0.15  # metric only, no page
  5m: 0.07   # page if sustained for 2m
  1h: 0.02   # immediate page
pager_mapping:
  30s: ticket_only
  5m: page_on_duration(2m)
  1h: page_immediate
suppress_errors: ["RedisConnectionTimeout", "RedisPoolExhausted"]
annotate_with: ["deploy.tag", "deploy.user"]
```

Raj (SRE): applying to staging: `monitorctl apply --env=staging --rule=slo_burnrate_high --patch=patch_v1`
Nina (on-call): Priya, confirm rollback finished?
Priya (ENG-PLATFORM): rollback completed @ 09:22:20 UTC, canary set to 0%. traffic back to stable pools. host-12 shows connection backlog clearing.
Tom (Support): updating tickets: told customers we saw a transient embed hiccup tied to an internal deploy and that engineers rolled back the change. asked them to reopen if it persists.
Nina (on-call): metrics now: 30s window dropped from 0.18 -> 0.06 within 40s of rollback; 5m sits ~0.05; 1h 0.018. No new 504 reports in last 10m.
DeployBot: ANNOTATION: deploy.tag=adaptive-batching-2026-03-15 added to alert 2179123456
Raj (SRE): follow-ups for post-incident tuning:
- create a dashboard tile for redis pool usage and per-shard backpressure correlated with deploy tags
- consider adjusting windows to 45s/4m/2h for embed route since spikes are short but impactful
- add deploy->alert correlation rule so deploys that correlate with SLO spikes automatically annotate and escalate to the deploy owner first
Nina (on-call): I'll create the post-incident ticket, attach runbook link runbooks/slo-burn-embed and the new dashboard mockups.
Priya (ENG-PLATFORM): PR opened to change canary rollout strategy to avoid single-host pressure: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/pulls/502 (includes host weight randomization)
Raj (SRE): I'll apply the alert mapping to prod after staging validation: `monitorctl apply --env=prod --rule=slo_burnrate_high --patch=patch_v1 --dry-run=false`
Nina (on-call): handing off watchdesk to Raj for 2 hours. If 5m or 1h windows page, escalate to me and Priya. I'm available for context.
Raj (SRE): taking handoff. will monitor redis metrics and ticket queue. scheduling a 30-min follow-up review in the incident board.
Tom (Support): will keep customers updated and close tickets if no new errors in 1h.
Nina (on-call): summary for postmortem: root cause = adaptive batching canary concentrated load on single host causing redis pool exhaustion -> transient 504s -> SLO burn. mitigation = rollback, suppress 30s pager, alert mapping patch, follow-up work on canary distribution and redis pool observability.
PagerBot: RESOLVED: slo_burnrate_high | status=suppressed_by_rule_patch | note="30s window demoted to ticket_only"
Nina (on-call): closing live coordination thread, will reopen if 5m/1h thresholds trigger again. thanks all :thumbsup:
